nahhas-irab:37-37.t:
«وَإِقامِ الصَّلاةِ»: one says أقام الصلاة إقامة ("he performed the prayer, a performing"). The original is إقوامة: the vowel of the wāw was transferred to the qāf, so the wāw turned into an alif; after it came [another] alif, and both were quiescent, so one of them was dropped, and the hāʾ [the feminine ending] was kept so that you would not drop it as well and thereby mutilate the word. When you put it in construct (iḍāfa), the muḍāf ilayhi took the place of the hāʾ, so dropping it became permissible; if you do not put it in construct, dropping it is not permissible. Do you not see that you say وعد عدة ("he promised, a promise"), and dropping the hāʾ is not permissible, because you have already dropped a wāw — the original being وعدة — but if you put it in construct, dropping the hāʾ becomes permissible. Al-Farrāʾ recited: [al-Basīṭ metre] 307-
إنّ الخليط أجدّوا البين فانجردوا ... وأخلفوك عد الأمر الّذي وعدوا
(The companions resolved in earnest on parting and hastened away, and broke with you the promise of the matter they had promised.)
He means عدة, and dropped the hāʾ because he put it in construct. «يَخافُونَ يَوْماً تَتَقَلَّبُ فِيهِ الْقُلُوبُ وَالْأَبْصارُ»: we have already mentioned this. It was said: its meaning is that the hearts of the wicked will turn about upon the Fire; and it was said: «تتقلّب» means they are roasted once and the Fire scorches them once [again].

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: «وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «أَعْمالُهُمْ» is a second mubtadaʾ. It may also be a badal (substitute) for «الذين», and the khabar (predicate) is then «كَسَرابٍ بِقِيعَةٍ يَحْسَبُهُ الظَّمْآنُ ماءً». If you lighten the hamza, you say «الظّمآن». [Translator's note: the printed text shows the same spelling الظّمآن for the lightened form; the intended form (presumably الظَّمَانُ, without the hamza) is not distinguished in the source.]

nahhas-irab:40-40.t:
«ظُلُماتٌ» is on the basis of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject). Whoever reads «ظلمات» [in the genitive] makes it a badal (substitute) for the first «ظلمات». One also says «ظلمات» [ẓulamāt] because of the lightness of the fatḥa, and «ظلمات» [ẓulmāt] to avoid the heaviness of the ḍamma. [Translator's note: the source prints these variants without the vowelling that distinguishes them; the readings in brackets are the ones evidently intended.]
«وَمَنْ لَمْ يَجْعَلِ اللَّهُ لَهُ نُوراً فَما لَهُ مِنْ نُورٍ»: Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] interpreted it as referring to this world, i.e. whoever Allah has not granted guidance to Islam will not be guided. Others interpreted it as referring to the Hereafter, i.e. whoever Allah has not granted a light on the Day of Resurrection will not find the way to Paradise.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t:
[«وَالطَّيْرُ» is nominative] as maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «من». [Translator's note: the beginning of this entry, naming the word discussed, is missing in the source; it evidently concerns «وَالطَّيْرُ صَافَّاتٍ».] Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: «والطير» [in the accusative] is also permissible, in the sense of "with the birds", but it has not been read so. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard him permit قمت وزيدا ("I stood up, and Zayd [with me]") in the sense of "with Zayd". He said: this is better than the nominative. He said: but if you say قمت أنا وزيد ("I myself and Zayd stood up"), the nominative is better, though the accusative is permissible.
«كُلٌّ قَدْ عَلِمَ صَلاتَهُ وَتَسْبِيحَهُ»: the meaning may be: "each — Allah knows its prayer and its glorification". From this angle, putting «كلّ» in the accusative is permissible according to the Basrans and the Kufans. Abū Isḥāq said: prayer belongs to human beings, and glorification belongs to others as well as to them. The meaning may also be: "each knows its own prayer and its glorification".

nahhas-irab:43-43.t:
«أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُزْجِي سَحاباً ثُمَّ يُؤَلِّفُ بَيْنَهُ»: it may be asked: «بين» ("between") is only used of two or more, so how does «بينه» ("between it") come here? The answer is that «بينه» here refers to the collective [mass] of clouds, as you say: الشجر حسن، وقد جلست بينه ("the trees are fine, and I sat among them"). There is another view: that «السحاب» is singular, yet it is permissible to say «بينه» because it comprises many pieces, as the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl metre] 308-
قفا نبك من ذكرى حبيب ومنزل ... بسقط اللّوى بين الدّخول فحومل
(Halt, the two of you, and let us weep at the memory of a beloved and a dwelling, at the edge of the winding sand between al-Dakhūl and Ḥawmal.)
He used «بين» with «الدخول», which is a single [place], because it comprises several spots. This is the view of the grammarians, except al-Aṣmaʿī, who claimed that this is not permissible and used to transmit it as «بين الدّخول وحومل» [with wāw instead of fāʾ].
Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read «فَتَرَى الْوَدْقَ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ خِلالِهِ» ] [i.e. من خَلَلِه]. [Translator's note: the source prints the standard reading «خِلالِهِ» followed by a stray bracket; the variant being described is evidently من خَلَلِه, as the following sentence shows.] خلل is the singular of خلال, like جمل and جمال; it is a singular that indicates a plural.
«وَيُنَزِّلُ مِنَ السَّماءِ مِنْ جِبالٍ فِيها مِنْ بَرَدٍ»: whoever says the meaning is "from mountains of hail in it", «برد» for him is in the position of the genitive (khafḍ) — this is what al-Farrāʾ says — as you say: الإنسان من لحم ودم ("man is of flesh and blood") and الإنسان لحم ودم ("man is flesh and blood"). On his view the meaning must be "from mountains, hail, in it", with tanwīn on «الجبال», because he said: the mountains are the hail. On the view of the Basrans, «من برد» is in the position of the accusative, and the genitive is also permissible, as you say: مررت بخاتم حديدا and بخاتم حديد ("I passed by a ring of iron"): the genitive is as a badal (substitute), and the accusative is, according to Sībawayh, as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and according to Abū al-ʿAbbās [al-Mubarrad] as explanation (bayān).
Whoever says the meaning is "from the quantity of mountains", «من برد» for him is in the position of the accusative and nothing else. Al-Farrāʾ said:
as you say عندي بيتان تبنا ("I have two houses' worth of straw"); and like it, in his view, is «أَوْ عَدْلُ ذلِكَ صِياماً» [al-Māʾida: 95]. Whoever says:
«من» is redundant (zāʾida) in both places, both are for him in the position of the accusative and nothing else.
Abū Jaʿfar [al-Qāriʾ] read «يَكادُ سَنا بَرْقِهِ يَذْهَبُ بِالْأَبْصارِ» with ḍamma on the yāʾ [i.e. يُذهِب]. Abū Ḥātim claimed that this is a solecism (laḥn), and this is the view of his teacher al-Akhfash: one says دخل بالمدخل ("he entered with the one entering"), and [al-Akhfash] does not permit أدخل here, and claims that the bāʾ alternates with the alif [of the causative form IV]. This is the clear view. But as for it being an error that is not permissible and cannot be accounted for — a group has claimed that the bāʾ may be redundant, and they cited as proof the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: «وَمَنْ يُرِدْ فِيهِ بِإِلْحادٍ بِظُلْمٍ» [al-Ḥajj: 25], although a view other than this is more appropriate than it, namely what ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān related to us from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad]. He said: the bāʾ is attached to the maṣdar (verbal noun), since the verb indicates it and is derived from it; on this basis the implied meaning is "its going away with the sights" or "its taking away [of the sights]". Likewise: أدخل بالمدخل السّجن الدار [sic] is permissible on this basis. [Translator's note: the example is printed as given; its wording appears garbled in the source.]

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: «يُقَلِّبُ اللَّهُ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهارَ» is figurative (majāz), i.e. He turns this into that and that into this; when one of them departs and the other enters, it is as though it were what [the first] was turned into.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t:
«وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَ كُلَّ دَابَّةٍ مِنْ ماءٍ»: [this is] the reading of the Medinans, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and the rest of the Kufans; [others] read «خالق كلّ دابّة» ("the Creator of every creature"). [Translator's note: as printed, the sentence attributes «خالق» to "the Medinans, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and the rest of the Kufans", which cannot be right, since these read «خَلَقَ»; «خالق» is the reading of Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī. The text appears to have lost a phrase; the bracketed words follow the evident sense.] Both meanings are sound: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has given two pieces of information, and it should not be said here that one of the two readings is more correct than the other, because they indicate two meanings. But if someone were to say: «خلق» is more frequent in this [kind of context], because it is not something specific — «خالق» is said in the general sense, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: «الْخالِقُ الْبارِئُ الْمُصَوِّرُ» [al-Ḥashr: 24], while in specific contexts [it is] «الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ» [al-Anʿām: 1], and likewise «هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ واحِدَةٍ» [al-Aʿrāf: 189] — then likewise it should be «وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَ كُلَّ دَابَّةٍ مِنْ ماءٍ».
«الدابّة» is every animal that creeps (dabba) upon the earth; one says دبّ, and he is داب, and the hāʾ is for intensiveness (mubālagha). It was said: by "water" here is meant semen, as He said: «مِنْ ماءٍ دافِقٍ» [al-Ṭāriq: 6]. It was said: since the creation of the earth was from water, this came thus. And it was said: the origin of the creation of fire and light is from water.
«فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِي عَلى بَطْنِهِ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِي عَلى رِجْلَيْنِ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِي عَلى أَرْبَعٍ»: whatever walks on more than four, walks on four. Rational beings were given precedence [in the use of «من»] when they were combined with non-rational ones, because they are the ones addressed and charged with worship.

nahhas-irab:49-49.t: «مُذْعِنِينَ» is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:50-50.t: «أَفِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ أَمِ ارْتابُوا»: Allah rebuked them for that, in view of the proofs He had made manifest, and said: «بَلْ أُولئِكَ هُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ».

nahhas-irab:51-51.t: Al-Ḥasan read «إِنَّما كانَ قَوْلَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ» [i.e. قولُ, in the nominative], making it the noun (ism) of «كان», with the khabar (predicate) being «أَنْ يَقُولُوا». [Translator's note: the source prints the standard vowelling «قَوْلَ» while describing al-Ḥasan's nominative reading.]

nahhas-irab:53-53.t:
«قُلْ لا تُقْسِمُوا»:
He forbade them from swearing, because their intention was otherwise, so they would be sinful if they swore. «طاعَةٌ مَعْرُوفَةٌ»
is on the basis of an implied "let there be obedience"; the meaning may also be: "obedience is more fitting for you".
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: «طاعة» in the accusative is permissible, meaning as a maṣdar (verbal noun) [i.e. mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)].

nahhas-irab:54-54.t: «فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا» is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) by the condition. The original is تتولّوا: one of the two tāʾs was dropped because the other indicates it, and the nūn was dropped for the jussive. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is in the fāʾ and what follows it.

nahhas-irab:55-55.t:
In this verse there is an indication of the prophethood of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, because Allah fulfilled that promise; and there is in it an indication of the caliphate of Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān and ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with them, because He did not appoint as successors any of those addressed by this verse other than them, since this verse was revealed before the conquest of Mecca.
It is reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "The caliphate after me is thirty [years]" — this is in accordance with the verse.
«وَلَيُبَدِّلَنَّهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ خَوْفِهِمْ أَمْناً»: ʿĀṣim reads «وَلَيُبَدِّلَنَّهُمْ» with the lighter form [i.e. وليُبْدِلنّهم]. Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm related from al-Farrāʾ that he said:
ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read «وَلَيُبَدِّلَنَّهُمْ» with the doubled form. This is a mistake about ʿĀṣim, and we have mentioned after it a mistake graver than it, namely that he reported the lighter form from the rest of the people. [Translator's note: the source prints «وَلَيُبَدِّلَنَّهُمْ» with shadda in all three places, so the light and doubled forms being contrasted are not distinguished in the printed text.] Abū Jaʿfar said: Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā [Thaʿlab] claimed that there is a difference between the lighter and the doubled form, and that one says بدّلته meaning "I changed it", and أبدلته meaning "I removed it and put something else [in its place]". Abū Jaʿfar said: this view is correct, as you say: أبدل لي هذا الدرهم, i.e. "remove it and give me another", and you say: قد بدّلت بعدنا, i.e. "you have changed [since we left]"; yet one of them is sometimes used in place of the other, though what he mentioned is more common.
«يَعْبُدُونَنِي» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); it may also be resumptive (mustaʾnaf), in the position of the nominative.

nahhas-irab:57-57.t:
«لا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مُعْجِزِينَ فِي الْأَرْضِ»: [«الذين» and «معجزين» are] two objects. Ḥamza read «لا يحسبنّ الذين كفروا معجزين في الأرض» [with yāʾ]. Abū Jaʿfar said: I know of no one among the people of Arabic grammar and lexicography, Basran or Kufan, who does not forbid reading this reading. Some of them say it is a solecism (laḥn), because only one object has come for «يحسبنّ»; among those who said this is Abū Ḥātim. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is weak, and he permitted it despite its weakness on the basis that the first object is omitted; the meaning according to him is: "let not those who disbelieve reckon themselves (إيّاهم) able to frustrate [Allah] in the earth", meaning "let them not reckon their own selves able to frustrate [Allah] in the earth".
I saw Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] incline to this view, I mean the view of al-Farrāʾ. And I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say about this reading: «الذي» [sic] is in the position of the accusative; he said: the meaning is: "let not the disbeliever reckon those who disbelieve able to frustrate [Allah] in the earth".

nahhas-irab:58-58.t:
«يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لِيَسْتَأْذِنْكُمُ الَّذِينَ مَلَكَتْ أَيْمانُكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ لَمْ يَبْلُغُوا الْحُلُمَ مِنْكُمْ ثَلاثَ مَرَّاتٍ مِنْ قَبْلِ صَلاةِ الْفَجْرِ وَحِينَ تَضَعُونَ ثِيابَكُمْ مِنَ الظَّهِيرَةِ وَمِنْ بَعْدِ صَلاةِ الْعِشاءِ ثَلاثُ عَوْراتٍ لَكُمْ لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلا عَلَيْهِمْ جُناحٌ بَعْدَهُنَّ طَوَّافُونَ عَلَيْكُمْ بَعْضُكُمْ عَلى بَعْضٍ كَذلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمُ الْآياتِ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ» (58)
Al-Ḥasan read «وَالَّذِينَ لَمْ يَبْلُغُوا الْحُلُمَ» with the lām made quiescent [i.e. الحُلْم], because of the heaviness of the ḍamma. The Medinans and Abū ʿAmr read «ثَلاثُ عَوْراتٍ» in the nominative, and the Kufans read (ثلاث عورات) in the accusative; what is said about this is close to what is said about «يحسبنّ». Abū Ḥātim said: the accusative is weak and rejected. Al-Farrāʾ said: the nominative is dearer to me. He said: I chose the nominative only because the meaning is "these traits are three [times of] privacy". The nominative according to al-Kisāʾī is by being the mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) according to him is what follows it. He did not say [that it is nominative] by the returning pronoun; he stated explicitly: by being the mubtadaʾ. He said: the ʿawrāt are the hours in which there is exposure and privacy — yet he read it in the accusative. There are two views on the accusative: one of them is that it refers back to His words «ثَلاثَ مَرَّاتٍ» [as a badal (substitute)], and for this reason al-Farrāʾ considered it far-fetched. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: the meaning is "let them ask your permission at the times of three [periods of] privacy". [Translator's note: the source announces two views on the accusative but only the first is explicitly numbered; al-Zajjāj's statement evidently represents the second.]
«طَوَّافُونَ» means "they are going round". Al-Farrāʾ said: as you say in ordinary speech: إنّما هم خدمكم وطوافون عليكم ("they are only your servants and those who go round among you"). Al-Farrāʾ ] permitted «طوافين» in the accusative [as a ḥāl (circumstantial)], because it is indefinite and the pronoun in «عليكم» is definite. The Basrans do not permit it to be a ḥāl from the pronoun from «الذين» [sic] in «عليكم» and in «بعضكم», because of the difference of the two governing words. It is not permissible [to say] مررت بزيد، ونزلت على عمرو العاقلين ("I passed by Zayd and stayed with ʿAmr, the two intelligent ones") as a naʿt (adjective) for both of them. [Translator's note: the source prints «نصب طوافون» with the nominative form and contains a stray bracket; the sentence on the pronoun is translated as written.]
«بَعْضُكُمْ عَلى بَعْضٍ لله» [sic] is with an implied verb, i.e. "some of you go round to others". [Translator's note: the word «لله» after the Quranic phrase appears to be an intrusion in the printed text.]
«كَذلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمُ الْآياتِ»: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, i.e. Allah makes clear to you His signs that indicate His oneness, with a making-clear like that by which He made these things clear to you.

nahhas-irab:59-59.t: Al-Ḥasan read «الحلم» [i.e. الحُلْم], dropping the ḍamma because of its heaviness. «فَلْيَسْتَأْذِنُوا», i.e. let them ask permission at all times. He did not say فليستأذنوكم ("let them ask your permission"), whereas He said in the first [verse] «لِيَسْتَأْذِنْكُمُ», because children are not addressed and not charged with worship ...

nahhas-irab:60-60.t:
«وَالْقَواعِدُ مِنَ النِّساءِ» is the plural of قاعد, without the hāʾ [the feminine ending]. There are three views on it: the doctrine of the Basrans is that it is by way of attribution (nasab) [i.e. "one characterised by sitting"]; the doctrine of the Kufans is that since it is applied only to the feminine, it has no need of the hāʾ; and the third view is that it came without the hāʾ to distinguish it from القاعدة in the sense of "the one sitting down".
«فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِنَّ جُناحٌ أَنْ يَضَعْنَ ثِيابَهُنَّ غَيْرَ مُتَبَرِّجاتٍ بِزِينَةٍ» is as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. they do not intend to display their adornment to men.

nahhas-irab:61-61.t:
«لَيْسَ عَلَى الْأَعْمى حَرَجٌ»: [«حرج»] is the noun (ism) of «ليس», and we have already mentioned it. Among the best of what has been said about it is that it concerns jihād. As for the meaning of «وَلا عَلى أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَنْ تَأْكُلُوا مِنْ بُيُوتِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ آبائِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ أُمَّهاتِكُمْ» to the end of the verse, there are three views on it: one is that this is permissible only after permission; another is that it was known that they would not begrudge them this; and the third view is that the verse is abrogated, and that this was at first, then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Your blood and your wealth are inviolable except with permission, and the inviolability of a Muslim's property is like the inviolability of his blood." From this it follows that nothing of anyone's property is lawful for anyone except with permission, or what the Muslims agree upon when one fears for one's life.
It has been said: the verse is abrogated by His words, Mighty and Majestic: «يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتاً غَيْرَ بُيُوتِكُمْ حَتَّى تَسْتَأْنِسُوا وَتُسَلِّمُوا عَلى أَهْلِها» [al-Nūr: 27]; if one may not enter except with permission, then with food it is even further [from permissible]. And He, Mighty and Majestic, said:
«يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتَ النَّبِيِّ إِلَّا أَنْ يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ إِلى طَعامٍ غَيْرَ ناظِرِينَ إِناهُ» [al-Aḥzāb: 53]. Even if there were nothing on the abrogation of the verse except the ḥadīth that Mālik related from Nāfiʿ from Ibn ʿUmar from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "None of you should milk his brother's livestock except with his permission. Would any of you like his storeroom to be come to, his store broken open and his food taken?" — that would suffice.
Qatāda read «مفتاحه» ("its key"), and it is a dialectal form; مفتح is more common in the speech of the Arabs, as is shown to you by its plural مفاتح.
«أَنْ تَأْكُلُوا جَمِيعاً»: [«جميعا»] is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
«تَحِيَّةً» is a maṣdar (verbal noun). Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: because the meaning of «فَسَلِّمُوا»
is "greet". Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ permitted «تحيّة» in the nominative, in the sense of "it is a greeting". «مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ»: because Allah commanded it. «مُبارَكَةً طَيِّبَةً»: because the one who hears it finds it pleasant to hear.

nahhas-irab:62-62.t:
«إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَإِذا كانُوا مَعَهُ عَلى أَمْرٍ جامِعٍ لَمْ يَذْهَبُوا حَتَّى يَسْتَأْذِنُوهُ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَسْتَأْذِنُونَكَ أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ فَإِذَا اسْتَأْذَنُوكَ لِبَعْضِ شَأْنِهِمْ فَأْذَنْ لِمَنْ شِئْتَ مِنْهُمْ وَاسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمُ اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ» (62)
«إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). «وَإِذا كانُوا مَعَهُ عَلى أَمْرٍ جامِعٍ», i.e. something in which nothing but gathering together is needed [sic], such as war and the like. [Translator's note: «ما يحتاج فيه إلا الاجتماع» is translated as written; the sense intended is presumably "something for which gathering together is needed".] «لَمْ يَذْهَبُوا حَتَّى يَسْتَأْذِنُوهُ», because he may need their presence.

nahhas-irab:63-63.t:
«لا تَجْعَلُوا دُعاءَ الرَّسُولِ بَيْنَكُمْ كَدُعاءِ بَعْضِكُمْ»: the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a second object.
«قَدْ يَعْلَمُ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ يَتَسَلَّلُونَ مِنْكُمْ لِواذاً»: [«لواذا»] is a maṣdar (verbal noun); it may also be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "taking cover with one another". Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: i.e. "going against [him]"; its real sense is that some of them take refuge (yalūdh) behind others, i.e. hide behind them so as not to be seen. One says لاوذ يلاوذ ملاوذة ولواذا, and لاذ يلوذ لوذا ولياذا: the wāw is changed to yāʾ because of the kasra before it, following لاذ in its weakness. When it is the maṣdar of fāʿala, it is not made weak, because fāʿala cannot be made weak.
«فَلْيَحْذَرِ الَّذِينَ يُخالِفُونَ عَنْ أَمْرِهِ أَنْ تُصِيبَهُمْ فِتْنَةٌ»: «أن» is in the position of the accusative by «يحذر». According to most grammarians حذر زيدا ("he was wary of Zayd") is not permissible, but with «أن» it is permissible, because prepositions are dropped with it. «عَنْ أَمْرِهِ أَنْ تُصِيبَهُمْ» [sic] is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). [Translator's note: this last statement is translated as printed; it does not fit the phrase quoted, and something appears to have dropped out of the source.]

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: (سُورَةٌ أَنْزَلْناها), in the sense «هذه سورةٌ» (this is a sūra). ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «سورةً أنزلناها» in the accusative, in the sense «أنزلنا سورةً» (We sent down a sūra). The meaning may also be «اتلُ سورةً أنزلناها» (recite a sūra that We sent down). (وَفَرَضْناها), that is, "and We prescribed in it [matters] of the lawful and the unlawful". On «وفرضناها» «[Translator's note: the second mention evidently refers to the variant «وفرّضناها» with the rāʾ doubled, which the printed text does not vowel.]» there are three views. Abū ʿAmr said: [it means] "We set it out in detail". It has been said: it is for multiplicity, because of the many obligations in it. The third view: al-Farrāʾ said: it means "We made it obligatory on you and on those after you".

nahhas-irab:2-2.t:
(الزَّانِيَةُ وَالزَّانِي فَاجْلِدُوا كُلَّ واحِدٍ مِنْهُما مِائَةَ جَلْدَةٍ): ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «الزانيةَ والزانيَ» in the accusative. This is the choice of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, may Allah have mercy on them both, because with a command the verb has more claim [to govern]. The rest of the grammarians disagree with them, and Muḥammad ibn Yazīd argued against them from the saying of Allah, Majestic and Mighty:
(وَالَّذانِ يَأْتِيانِها مِنْكُمْ) [al-Nisāʾ: 16]. The argument for the nominative is that two particular individuals who committed fornication are not meant, so that it would be made accusative; since it is indefinite, the nominative is required in it, on three bases: the view of Sībawayh is that the meaning is «وفيما فُرض عليكم الزانيةُ والزاني» (and among what has been prescribed for you: the fornicatress and the fornicator); and it has been said: by what refers back to it. (وَلا تَأْخُذْكُمْ بِهِما رَأْفَةٌ), and «رَآفة» «[Translator's note: the printed text does not vowel the variant; from the explanation it is «رَآفة» on the pattern «فَعالة».]», because «فَعالة» is common in [words for] qualities, such as «القَباحة» (ugliness); and «فَعْلة» is according to the original form.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: (الزَّانِي لا يَنْكِحُ إِلاَّ زانِيَةً أَوْ مُشْرِكَةً وَالزَّانِيَةُ لا يَنْكِحُها إِلاَّ زانٍ أَوْ مُشْرِكٌ وَحُرِّمَ ذلِكَ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) (3): (الزَّانِي لا يَنْكِحُ إِلَّا زانِيَةً أَوْ مُشْرِكَةً): we have already mentioned its meaning, and that the right view about it is that it is abrogated. «وحرّم ذلك»: that a man marry a fornicatress and a woman a fornicator.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: Abū Zurʿa ibn ʿAmr ibn Jarīr read «ثُمَّ لم يأتوا بأربعةٍ شهداءَ» «[Translator's note: the printed text gives the reading in the standard form (بِأَرْبَعَةِ شُهَداءَ); the analyses that follow show it is «بأربعةٍ» with tanwīn.]». There are three analyses of it: «شهداء» may be in the position of genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of «أربعة»; it may be in the position of accusative, in the sense «ثم لم يُحضِروا أربعةً شهداءَ» (then they did not bring four as witnesses); and the third is that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the indefinite noun. (وَلا تَقْبَلُوا لَهُمْ شَهادَةً أَبَداً وَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْفاسِقُونَ).

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تابُوا): [«الذين»] is in the position of accusative as the excepted (mustathnā); it may also be in the position of genitive as a badal (substitute). The meaning is: "Do not ever accept testimony from them, except those who repent."

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: (وَالَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ أَزْواجَهُمْ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُمْ شُهَداءُ إِلَّا أَنْفُسُهُمْ): [«أنفسهم» is nominative] as a badal (substitute); and the accusative [is possible] as the excepted and as the khabar of «يكن». (فَشَهادَةُ أَحَدِهِمْ أَرْبَعَ شَهاداتٍ بِاللَّهِ) in the accusative is the reading of the people of Medina and Abū ʿAmr; the reading of the Kufans is (أَرْبَعُ شَهاداتٍ بِاللَّهِ) in the nominative, as mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), that is: "the testimony of one of them that removes from him the penalty of the slanderer is four testimonies", as you say: "the noon prayer is four rakʿas". The accusative is because the meaning of «شهادة» is «أن شهد» (that he testify), so the implied form is «فعليهم أن يشهد أحدُهم أربعَ شهادات» (it is incumbent on them that one of them testify four testimonies), or «فالأمرُ أن يشهد أحدُهم أربعَ شهادات».

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: (وَالْخامِسَةُ) is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is «أنّ» and its ṣila (relative clause). The meaning of the lightened [«أنْ»] is like the meaning of the heavy one, because its meaning is «أنّه». Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Ṭalḥa read «والخامسةَ أنّ» in the accusative, in the sense "and he testifies the fifth testimony".

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: (وَلَوْلا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ): [«فضل»] is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) according to Sībawayh, and the khabar (predicate) is omitted; the Arabs do not express it. (وَرَحْمَتُهُ) is conjoined to it. (وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ تَوَّابٌ حَكِيمٌ) is also conjoined to it. The apodosis of «لولا» is omitted because the like of it is mentioned afterwards. Allah said: (وَلَوْلا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ فِي الدُّنْيا وَالْآخِرَةِ لَمَسَّكُمْ فِيما أَفَضْتُمْ فِيهِ عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ).

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ جاؤُ بِالْإِفْكِ): [«الذين»] is the noun (ism) of «إنّ»; (عُصْبَةٌ) is its khabar (predicate). The accusative of «عصبة» as a ḥāl (circumstantial) is also permissible, the khabar then being (لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مِنْهُمْ مَا اكْتَسَبَ مِنَ الْإِثْمِ). Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj and Yaʿqūb read «والذي تولّى كُبْرَه» with ḍamma on the kāf. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is a good option, because the Arabs say:
«فلانٌ تولّى عُظْمَ كذا وكذا» (so-and-so took on the greater part of such-and-such) «[Translator's note: the printed text has «أولى» for «تولّى».]», that is, most of it. Abū Jaʿfar said: what he adduced is no proof, because one thing may have the meaning of another while the vowelling in it differs. The better known in the speech of the Arabs in such a case is «الكِبْر», and «الكُبْر» is [used] in lineage; one says: «الولاءُ للكُبْر» (clientage goes to the eldest).

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: (لَوْلا إِذْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ ظَنَّ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتُ بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ خَيْراً), that is, of their brethren. (وَقالُوا هذا إِفْكٌ مُبِينٌ): so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made it obligatory on the Muslims, when they hear a man slander someone or mention him with something ugly for which they do not know him, to reproach him and call him a liar; and He threatened whoever neglects that and whoever passes it on.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: (إِذْ تَلَقَّوْنَهُ بِأَلْسِنَتِكُمْ): the original is «تتلقّونه», that is, some of you take it from others and some of you accept it from others; its like is (فَتَلَقَّى آدَمُ مِنْ رَبِّهِ كَلِماتٍ) [al-Baqara: 37]. It is related from ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that she read «إذ تَلِقُونَه» «[Translator's note: the printed text gives her reading in the standard form (تَلَقَّوْنَهُ); the explanation that follows shows it is «تَلِقُونَه».]»; its isnād is sound, and it is known to have no source except from the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar al-Jumaḥī. Both meanings are sound, because they both received it and spread it hastily (وَلَقُوه). The original is «تَوْلِقونه»; the wāw was dropped in conformity with «يَلِق». One says «وَلَقَ يَلِقُ» when one is quick in lying; its derivation is from «الوَلْق», which is lightness and speed.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: (يَعِظُكُمُ اللَّهُ أَنْ تَعُودُوا): [«أن تعودوا»] is in the position of accusative.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, threatened them for wanting depravity, that is, spreading indecency among those who believe. (وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ), that is, He knows the extent of the enormity of this sin and the requital for it, and He knows everything.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: It «[Translator's note: the word meant is (زَكى), as the following quotation shows.]» is of the roots with final wāw, even though it is written with yāʾ. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on him, concerning His saying (وَلَوْلا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ ما زَكى مِنْكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ أَبَداً): he said: none of the creatures would have been guided to anything by which he benefits himself or by which he removes what he wards off from himself.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: (وَلا يَأْتَلِ أُولُوا الْفَضْلِ مِنْكُمْ): the yāʾ was dropped for the jussive. Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ and Zayd ibn Aslam read «ولا يتألَّ أولو الفضل», the alif dropped for the jussive. The meaning is the same, as you say: «فلان يتكسّب» and «يكتسب» (so-and-so earns).

nahhas-irab:23-23.t:
Among the best of what has been said about this is that it is general to all people who slander, male and female; the implied form is:
«الذين يرمون الأنفسَ المحصنات» (those who accuse chaste souls), so male and female are included in this. Likewise in «الذين يرمون», except that the masculine was given precedence over the feminine.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: Mujāhid read «يومئذٍ يوفّيهم اللهُ دينَهم الحقُّ» «[Translator's note: the printed text vowels the reading in the standard form (دِينَهُمُ الْحَقَّ); the description shows «الحقُّ» in the nominative.]», putting «الحقّ» in the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of Allah, Majestic and Mighty. Abū ʿUbayd said: Were it not for the aversion to differing from the people, the right option would be the nominative, so that it be a naʿt of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and agree with the reading of Ubayy; that is because Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim said: I saw in the codex of Ubayy «يوفّيهم اللهُ الحقُّ دينَهم». This statement of Abū ʿUbayd's is not acceptable, because he argued for something that contradicts the great majority. Nor is there any proof in it, because even if it were sound that it is so in the codex of Ubayy, the reading could be «يومئذ يوفّيهم اللهُ الحقَّ دينَهم», with «دينهم» a badal (substitute) for «الحقّ». Moreover, in the reading of the generality, (دِينَهُمُ الْحَقَّ), «الحقّ» is a naʿt of «دينهم», and the meaning is good, because Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has mentioned the evildoers, so He made known that He requites them with what is due (الحقّ), as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: (وَهَلْ نُجازِي إِلَّا الْكَفُورَ) [Sabaʾ: 17]; for Allah's requital, Majestic and Mighty, of the disbeliever and the evildoer is with what is due and with justice, and His requital of those who do good is with bounty and beneficence.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t:
(الْخَبِيثاتُ لِلْخَبِيثِينَ وَالْخَبِيثُونَ لِلْخَبِيثاتِ): we have mentioned several views on it. Among the best of what has been said about it:
that the meaning is "fornicators are for fornicators", according to how the [religious] obligation stood at the beginning «[Translator's note: the printed text reads «على ما كان التعبّد مبرئا», which appears corrupt; «مبتدأ» (at the beginning) is assumed here.]».

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: (لا تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتاً غَيْرَ بُيُوتِكُمْ حَتَّى تَسْتَأْنِسُوا): ʿIkrima said: that is, until you ask permission. Its literal meaning in the language is "until you find out", derived from «آنستُ الشيءَ», that is, I perceived it «[Translator's note: the printed text has «تستعملوا … استعملته» (make use of … I made use of it), apparently a corruption of «تستعلموا … استعلمته» (find out … I found it out).]». (ذلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ), that is, than entering without asking permission, because of the suspicion that it involves. (لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ), that is, so that you take heed of what is beneficial for you.

nahhas-irab:30-31.t:
(قُلْ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَغُضُّوا مِنْ أَبْصارِهِمْ): «مِن» here is for clarifying the genus (bayān al-jins), and likewise (يَغْضُضْنَ مِنْ أَبْصارِهِنَّ). The doubled letter appears [unassimilated] in the second, because the final radical in the second is vowelless and in the first is vowelled; both are in the position of jussive as an apodosis (jawāb). The implied form according to al-Māzinī is «قل للمؤمنين غُضّوا يَغُضّوا» (say to the believers: lower [your gazes], and they will lower). (وَيَحْفَظُوا فُرُوجَهُمْ): Abū al-ʿĀliya said: that is, so that no one sees them. Others said: so Allah also forbade the Muslims to enter a bathhouse without a waist-wrapper. The Muslims agree that the two private parts are ʿawra (what must be covered) in a man, and that the whole of a woman is ʿawra except her face and her hands, about which they differed. Most scholars said concerning the man: from his navel to his knee is ʿawra, which may not be seen. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَبِيرٌ بِما يَصْنَعُونَ):
the noun (ism) of «إنّ» and its khabar (predicate). (وَلْيَضْرِبْنَ بِخُمُرِهِنَّ عَلى جُيُوبِهِنَّ): «ولِيضربن» with kasra on the lām is permissible, and that is the original; the kasra was dropped because of its heaviness. «يضربن» is in the position of jussive by the command, except that it is indeclinable (mabnī), on one and the same form, following the past tense, according to Sībawayh. The meaning is: let them draw their «خُمُر», which are the head-coverings, close over their bosoms, lest their breasts or necks show. The sound [transmission] of the Kufans' reading is «على جِيوبهنّ» «[Translator's note: the printed text vowels it in the standard form (جُيُوبِهِنَّ); the comparison with «بيوتاً» shows the kasra reading «جِيوبهنّ» is meant.]», just as they read «بِيوتاً». The early grammarians do not allow this reading; they say: «بَيْت / بُيوت» is like «فَلْس / فُلوس». Abū Isḥāq said: it is permissible on the basis that a kasra is substituted for the ḍamma. As for what is related from Ḥamza, combining the ḍamma and the kasra, it is impossible; no one can pronounce it except by gesturing towards what is not permissible. (أَوِ التَّابِعِينَ غَيْرِ أُولِي الْإِرْبَةِ): Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ, ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir read «أو التابعين غيرَ», with «غير» in the accusative as an exception. Abū Ḥātim said: [it is accusative] as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The genitive is as a naʿt (adjective), even though the first is definite, because it is not specifically aimed at [a particular group]; and if you wish you may say it is a badal (substitute). Its parallel is (غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ) [al-Fātiḥa: 7], in both the genitive and the accusative. (أَوِ الطِّفْلِ) in the sense of «الأطفال» (children); the proof of that is its being described by «الذين»: (الَّذِينَ لَمْ يَظْهَرُوا عَلى عَوْراتِ). Al-Farrāʾ related that the dialect of Qays is «عَوَرات» with fatḥa on the wāw; this is the analogical form, because it is not an adjective, as you say «جَفْنة / جَفَنات»; except that the sukūn is better in «عورات» and the like, because when the wāw is vowelled and what precedes it is vowelled, it is changed into an alif, and were this done the meaning would be lost. Al-Kisāʾī related «أَيُّهُ المؤمنون» «[Translator's note: the printed text vowels it in the standard form (أَيُّهَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ); the description shows «أيُّهُ».]» with ḍamma on the hāʾ; this is an anomalous dialect with no justification, because «ها» is for drawing attention.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: (وَأَنْكِحُوا الْأَيامى مِنْكُمْ): [«الأيامى»] is the plural of «أيِّم»; according to the lexicographers «الأيِّم» is a woman who has no husband, whether a virgin or previously married. Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, al-Kisāʾī and others related this. That is clear in His saying, Majestic and Mighty, (وَأَنْكِحُوا الْأَيامى مِنْكُمْ), for He did not permit a previously married woman to the exclusion of a virgin; and the ḥadīth of the Prophet ﷺ "The «أيِّم» has more right over herself" is from exactly this. The plural of «أيِّم» is «أيامى», «أيايم» and «إيام», like «جيِّد / جياد». The broken plural of «أمة» (slave-woman) is «إماء» and «آمٍ», and in the accusative «رأيتُ آمِياً»; and «إموان», like «أخ / إخوان», because the original of «أمة» is «أَمَوة», and in the sound plural «أَمَوات». Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: Hishām related «أَمَيات». He said: this is a mistake, because it is of the roots with final wāw. Al-Ḥasan read «والصالحين من عبيدكم»; «عبيد» is a noun of collectivity (ism jamʿ), not a regular plural; the regular plurals are «أعبُد» and «عِباد». Parallel to «عبيد» in being a noun of collectivity is their saying «معبوداء» and «عِبِدّى». Al-Farrāʾ said: «والصالحين من عبادكم وإماءَكم» in the accusative is permissible, construing it back on «الصالحين». (إِنْ يَكُونُوا فُقَراءَ يُغْنِهِمُ اللَّهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ) is a condition and its apodosis (jawāb). It has been said: He will enrich them through marriage; and this is sound in the language, because «فقير» (needy) is only understood relative to something, so one says: needy of food, needy of clothing, needy of marriage.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: (وَالَّذِينَ يَبْتَغُونَ الْكِتابَ): [«الذين»] is in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); and in the position of accusative, according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, by an implied verb, because after it there is a command.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t:
(اللَّهُ نُورُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). Its implied form is «اللهُ ذو نورِ السماوات والأرض» (Allah is the Possessor of the light of the heavens and the earth), like (وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ) [Yūsuf: 82]. (مَثَلُ نُورِهِ كَمِشْكاةٍ فِيها مِصْباحٌ) is also a mubtadaʾ and its khabar.
We have already mentioned its meaning. Shamir ibn ʿAṭiyya related from Kaʿb concerning the saying of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, (مَثَلُ نُورِهِ): he said: His light is Muḥammad ﷺ. Abū Jaʿfar said: because Muḥammad ﷺ, in his making things clear to the people, is like the light that illuminates for them. Kaʿb said: (كَمِشْكاةٍ): like a niche in which there is a lamp. He said: (الْمِصْباحُ) is the heart of Muḥammad ﷺ; (فِي زُجاجَةٍ): he said: (الزُّجاجَةُ) is his breast; (كَأَنَّها كَوْكَبٌ دُرِّيٌّ) refers to his breast. Then he returned to the lamp, which is in the heart, and said: (يُوقَدُ مِنْ شَجَرَةٍ مُبارَكَةٍ زَيْتُونَةٍ لا شَرْقِيَّةٍ وَلا غَرْبِيَّةٍ): he said: neither the sun of the east nor the sun of the west strikes it. (شَرْقِيَّةٍ) is a naʿt (adjective) of «زيتونة»; (وَلا) does not intervene [in government] between the adjective and what it qualifies; (وَلا غَرْبِيَّةٍ) is conjoined. (يَكادُ زَيْتُها يُضِيءُ): Kaʿb said:
It almost becomes clear to whoever sees Muḥammad ﷺ that he is a prophet, even if he does not speak, because of the signs placed upon him ﷺ, just as this oil almost gives light even if no fire touches it.
«درّي» has been read in four ways:
Al-Ḥasan and the people of the two Sanctuaries read (كَأَنَّها كَوْكَبٌ دُرِّيٌّ) with ḍamma on the dāl and the yāʾ doubled; while Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab — he and Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī, Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim and Qatāda — read «كأنّها كوكبٌ دَرِّيٌّ» with fatḥa on the dāl and the yāʾ doubled; Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read «كأنّها كوكبٌ دِرِّيءٌ» with kasra on the dāl and with hamza; and Ḥamza read «كأنّها كوكبٌ دُرِّيءٌ» with ḍamma on the dāl and with hamza. «[Translator's note: the printed text does not mark the vowels of the variants; they are given as the descriptions specify.]» These are four readings. Al-Farrāʾ related that one says «دِرِّيّ» with kasra on the dāl and the yāʾ doubled, without hamza. Abū Jaʿfar said:
The first reading is clear: the star is attributed to «الدُّرّ» (pearls). If someone says: but the star has more light than the pearl «[Translator's note: the printed text reads «فالكوكب نورا من الدّرّ», which appears defective; the objection is rendered according to its evident sense.]», it is said to him: the meaning is only that the excellence of this star over the other stars is like the excellence of the pearl over all other beads.
The second reading has this meaning, with a fatḥa substituted for the ḍamma, because the relative adjective (nisba) is a domain of change. The third reading, that of Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī, Abū ʿUbayd judged very weak, because he interpreted it from «درأتُ», that is, I pushed — that is, a star that runs from horizon to horizon. If the interpretation were as he interpreted it, there would be no point in the speech, and this star would have no distinction over most stars. Do you not see that one does not say "a human being of the sons of Adam came to me"? It is not fitting that such a far-fetched interpretation be attributed to the likes of Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī, may Allah have mercy on them both, given their standing and eminence. Rather, the interpretation on their behalf is what is related from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd: that their meaning in it is a star surging forth with light, as one says «اندرأ الحريق», that is, the fire surged forth; and this is a sound interpretation of this reading. Al-Akhfash Saʿīd ibn Masʿada related that one says «درأ الكوكبُ بضوئه» when its light extends and rises high.
As for the reading of Ḥamza, the lexicographers all, except the fewest of them, say: it is a solecism and not permissible, because there is no noun in the speech of the Arabs on the pattern «فُعِّيل». Abū ʿUbayd raised an objection about this and argued for Ḥamza, saying: it is not «فُعِّيل»; it is only «فُعُّول», like «سُبُّوح», with yāʾ substituted for the wāw, as they said «عُتِيّ». Abū Jaʿfar said: This objection and argument is among the greatest and gravest of mistakes, because this is not permissible at all; were what he said permissible, one would say «سُبِّيح» for «سُبُّوح», and no one says that.
«عُتِيّ» is not of this kind, and the difference between them is clear and evident, because «عتيّ» must be one of two things:
either it is the plural of «عاتٍ», in which case the substitution in it is necessary, because the plural is a domain of change, and a wāw does not occur at the end of nouns preceded by a ḍamma; since before this [wāw] there is a vowelless letter, and before the vowelless letter a ḍamma, and the vowelless letter is not a strong barrier, a kasra was substituted for the ḍamma and the wāw was changed into yāʾ. And if «عتيّ» is a singular, it would be more fitting with the wāw, and was before it because it is final «[Translator's note: this clause is garbled in the printed text and is rendered literally.]»; while the wāw in «فُعُّول» is not final, and changing it is not permissible. Whoever argued for Ḥamza with something resembling [a precedent] said: «مُرِّيق» has occurred, and it is «فُعِّيل». The truth in this is that «مرّيق» is foreign. What al-Farrāʾ related — the kasra of the dāl — is permissible, on the basis that a kasra is substituted for the ḍamma.
(يُوقَدُ مِنْ شَجَرَةٍ مُبارَكَةٍ) has been read in four ways. Al-Ḥasan, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, Mujāhid, Abū Jaʿfar and Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ read «تَوَقَّدَ من شجرة», with fatḥa on the dāl, making it a past verb; Shayba and Nāfiʿ read (يُوقَدُ مِنْ شَجَرَةٍ مُبارَكَةٍ). These two readings are close to each other, because both refer to the lamp, and that fits this description better, because it is what shows and gives light, while the glass is only a container for it. «تَوَقَّدَ» is the past verb of «تَوَقَّدَ يَتَوَقَّدُ», and «يُوقَدُ» is the imperfect verb of «أوقد يوقد». Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim read «تَوَقَّدُ»; the original according to his reading is «تَتَوَقَّدُ», and one of the two tāʾs was dropped because the other indicates it. The Kufans read «تُوقَدُ». «[Translator's note: the printed text does not mark the vowels of these variants; they are given as the descriptions specify.]» These two readings are on the basis of the feminine of «الزجاجة». (وَلَوْ لَمْ تَمْسَسْهُ نارٌ) is on the basis of the feminine of «النار»; Abū ʿUbayd claimed that he knew only this reading. Abū Ḥātim related that al-Suddī related from Abū Mālik from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read «ولو لم يمسسه نار» with the yāʾ.
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: the masculine is on the basis that it is a non-real feminine; and such, according to him, is the way of inanimate things.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t:
(فِي بُيُوتٍ أَذِنَ اللَّهُ أَنْ تُرْفَعَ): we have already discussed it. It has been said: the meaning is "pray in houses". ʿĀṣim and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir read «يُسَبَّحُ له فيها بالغُدُوّ والآصال» «[Translator's note: the printed text vowels it in the standard active form (يُسَبِّحُ); the discussion shows the passive «يُسَبَّحُ» is meant.]», and likewise it is related from al-Ḥasan. Sībawayh mentioned the like of this and recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 306-
ليبك يزيد ضارع لخصومة
(Let Yazīd be wept for — [let] one humbled in a quarrel [weep for him].)
The implied form is «يُسَبَّحُ له فيها رجالٌ» (He is glorified in them — men [glorify Him]), by implying this verb; because when He said «يُسبَّح», it indicated that there are those who glorify. On this basis you say «ضُرِبَ زيدٌ عمرٌو» (Zayd was struck — ʿAmr [struck him]): when you said «ضُرِبَ زيدٌ»,
it indicated that he had someone who struck him, so you mentioned him and implied a verb for him.
